subject: Do observations of the same individual at more than one site violate assumptions of a single-season occupancy model?

messages.author: 1195ce743af3d0d7
messages.subject: Do observations of the same individual at more than one site violate assumptions of a single-season occupancy model?
parts:
I vaguely remember seeing something that said observations of the same individual at more than one site during the same sampling occasion violates the assumptions of occupancy models. Is this true? 

If so, what assumption is violated? Is it closure? And what articles can I reference about this?

Thanks!

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Do observations of the same individual at more than one site violate assumptions of a single-season occupancy model?
parts:
Dear Cody,

I would say that it does (a little). Not closure, but the assumption of independence of occupancy status among sites. But unless this is likely to happen often, I would not care too much: in the history of statistics and ecology there has never been any assumption that is always totally met.

So the important thing usually is that an assumption is not violated too much or too often. Of course, this is a judgment call to some degree. Individuals moving among neighbouring sites will induce residual spatial autocorrelation in occupancy, i.e., a spatial pattern that cannot be explained by covariates. If you are worried about spatial autocorrelation in occupancy, you could fit an occupancy model with CAR prior e.g. in Win/OpenBUGS or use the R package stocc.

Best regards  --  Marc

parts:
Thanks for the answer!

I'm actually using the Integrated SDM developed by Bob Dorazio, that uses an occupancy-like framework and allows for the dual use of presence-only and detection/non-detection data. I'm aware of a paper by Pacifici where they develop this integrated framework to include spatial autocorrelation. So it sounds like I should try that. 

However, because my data comes from several years, it would be interesting to further develop this model to account for spatio-temporal autocorrelation.

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Do observations of the same individual at more than one site violate assumptions of a single-season occupancy model?
parts:
Hi Cody,

OK, but in this case, you would have to move from likelihood inference (that's what Bob Dorazio presents, right ?) to Bayes, since to account for spatial autocorrelation you have to go down the MCMC avenue. Unless you are very interested in this, I would not do this right now perhaps, because you would have to translate the Dorazio model into BUGS.

Most ecological data analyses do not account for all likely sources of dependence in the data, absolutely most. So unless you have serious worries about such an "overlap" in the detection radii of your sites I would simply ignore this.

About spatio-temporal autocorrelation: of course, but while spatial autocorrelation is typically just a nuisance, temporal autocorrelation is not: it's population dynamics mostly that is responsible for the latter and this of course is very much at the center of interest of an ecological study. So best to parametrize temporal autocorrelation in a biological meaningful manner, i.e., with some population model.

Best regards  --- Marc
